notes.content: Bachelor of Arts Major in French Concentration in French Studies

Students must complete a minimum of 120 units with a Pacific cumulative and major/program grade point average of 2.0 in order to earn the bachelor of arts degree with a major in French and a concentration in French studies.

notes.content: Breadth Requirement (7 courses, at least 3 units each)

Notes: 1) No more than 2 courses from a single discipline can be used to meet the Breadth Requirement. 2) Students must complete 60 units outside the primary discipline of the first major regardless of the department who offers the course(s) in that discipline. (This includes general education courses, transfer courses, CPCE/EXTN units, internships, etc.)

notes.content: Notes: 1) FREN 051 or FREN 120 may be taken in English to count towards one of the five courses above. 2) Two of the advanced courses may be completed in a study abroad program. 3) Other courses may be negotiable with a French advisor. 4) At least one semester of study abroad in a French speaking country is strongly urged.

Notes: 

1) FREN 051 or FREN 120 may be taken in English to count towards one of the five courses above. 

2) Two of the advanced courses may be completed in a study abroad program.

 3) Other courses may be negotiable with a French advisor. 

4) At least one semester of study abroad in a French speaking country is strongly urged.

notes.text: Bachelor of Arts Major in French Concentration in French Studies

Students must complete a minimum of 120 units with a Pacific cumulative and major/program grade point average of 2.0 in order to earn the bachelor of arts degree with a major in French and a concentration in French studies.

For more details, see General Education
Minimum 28 units and 9 courses that include:

Notes:
1) CORE Seminars cannot be taken for Pass/No Credit. 
2) Transfer students with 28 or more transfer credits taken after high school are exempt from both CORE seminars.
Breadth Requirement (7 courses, at least 3 units each)

Notes:
1) No more than 2 courses from a single discipline can be used to meet the Breadth Requirement.
2) Students must complete 60 units outside the primary discipline of the first major regardless of the department who offers the course(s) in that discipline. (This includes general education courses, transfer courses, CPCE/EXTN units, internships, etc.)

Notes: 
1) FREN 051 or FREN 120 may be taken in English to count towards one of the five courses above. 
2) Two of the advanced courses may be completed in a study abroad program.
 3) Other courses may be negotiable with a French advisor. 
4) At least one semester of study abroad in a French speaking country is strongly urged.
